children: Macy's raised its guidance for a second time this year after recording growth across its brands.
The department-store retailer lifted its full-year net sales outlook to $21.68 billion to $21.83 billion, from its previous outlook in June of $21.5 billion to $21.75 billion.
It now expects adjusted earnings per share to be $2.15 to $2.35, up from $2 to $2.20.
Profit for the second quarter was $169 million, or 62 cents a share, compared with $87 million, or 31 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted per-share earnings were 63 cents, ahead of the 37 cents anticipated by analysts, according to FactSet.
Net sales in the second quarter rose 1.1% to $4.87 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast sales of $4.81 billion.

Same-store sales rose 2.7%, ahead of the 1% growth analysts were projecting. That was driven by 1.1% same-store sales growth at Macy's core stores, 11.3% growth at Bloomingdale's and 6.2% at Bluemercury.
Bloomingdale's was a bright spot for the company once again, with sales volume hitting its highest second-quarter level in the brand's history.
Macy's received $98 million in tariff refunds during the quarter, plus another $18 million after the quarter ended. About $20 million of the total proceeds will flow to full-year earnings per share.
The remaining $96 million in refunds will be invested this year to support the company's multi-year turnaround strategy.
